title: dumpex v2 structured output (schema_version 2.4)
description: Validates the v2 envelope written by the six recon commands (--list/--modules/--threads/--pid/--sysinfo/--peb), --diff, --extract, --strings, --report, and --hunt, via --json. v2.4 adds `result.kind == "hunt"` and its hunterRecord/huntSummary (plus the finding/huntRegionRef/huntThreadRef/huntThreadRegionHit/huntPeHeaderHit/*Details supporting types) and meta.rules/meta.yara_rules, on top of v2.3's unchanged root shape and existing record types -- dumpex-output-v2.3.schema.json remains frozen and installable for validating output produced before this addition (it does NOT include "hunt" in its own result.kind enum: a closed enum's already-shipped copy must never start silently accepting a value it didn't originally define); no currently-produced document from any prior command is rejected by v2.4 beyond the schema_version string itself. `result.kind` is scoped to what has actually been migrated onto v2 so far; it grows as more commands migrate, it is not left open-ended. result.data.records[] items ARE typed per kind (see the allOf/if-then block in $defs/result and the record $defs) -- additionalProperties: false on every record type, so a dropped/renamed/retyped field or a stray field from the wrong kind fails validation, not just 'is an array'. dumpex-output-v1.1.schema.json remains the contract for any --hunt output NOT produced through the v2 envelope (unchanged until the CLI's atomic switch onto v2 -- see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md).

evidence.description: One entry per evidence source. A single-dump recon command emits exactly one entry (role: 'primary'); a comparison command emits one per side (e.g. 'baseline'/'target').

rules.description: rules.yaml provenance for this run -- matches dumpex.rules_pkg.loader.get_rules_source_info()'s return shape. Omitted entirely (not present as a key at all) when get_rules() was never called this run (e.g. --hunt injection alone never reads rules.yaml) -- see dumpex.output.envelope._rules_meta. `path`/`sha256` are only null for the built-in defaults (no file was loaded at all); `path` is basename-only under --redact-paths, matching every other path-bearing meta field's own redaction rule. `version` has no lower bound -- rules_pkg.loader only type-checks a rules.yaml-declared `version:` field, never its sign (see loader.py's own _validate_top_level), so this schema does not invent a constraint the Python side doesn't enforce. `path == null` is EXACTLY the built-in-defaults shape (dumpex.rules_pkg.loader's own hardcoded fallback dict, verified against _load_rules()'s only path==None assignment) -- sha256/explicit/version are pinned to null/false/1 on that branch, not merely nullable.

yara_rules.description: YARA rule-file provenance for this run -- matches dumpex.hunt.yara_hunt.get_yara_provenance()'s return shape. Omitted entirely when YARA scanning was never invoked this run (e.g. --hunt injection alone never loads any .yar/.yara file) -- see dumpex.output.envelope._yara_rules_meta. `rules_dir` is basename-only under --redact-paths. `aggregate_sha256` is never null in this branch -- load_and_compile() always calls hashlib.sha256().hexdigest() unconditionally (even over zero rule files), which never returns null; only the error-only branch below omits it entirely.

hexAddress.description: A memory address/pointer/handle, normalized to a fixed-width (16 hex digit), lowercase, 0x-prefixed string -- or null when there is nothing to report an address for (see dumpex/output/records.py's hex_address()). Never a bare int (uint64 precision isn't safe across all JSON consumers) and never a variable-width string.

module_context.description: resolved: backed by a known module. unregistered: ModuleListStream was available and this address is confirmed NOT backed by any known module (a real DFIR signal). unavailable: ModuleListStream itself is missing -- can't tell either way, must not be confused with 'unregistered'. null: start_address is itself unknown (module context is moot).

extractRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ExtractRecord.to_dict() -- the READ-side facts for one --extract invocation. `requested_address`/`requested_size` are never null -- a successful --extract always knows the exact address/size it read (unlike most other hexAddress-typed fields in this schema, which stay nullable for genuinely optional cases). NOT expressed here (Python-only, see ExtractRecord.__post_init__): bytes_read must never exceed requested_size -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES against each other within one object.

stringRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.StringRecord.to_dict() -- one extracted string from a --strings scan or a --report triage card's own Section 4 (notable_strings). `offset` is a plain byte offset relative to the read region's start, NOT a process address. Unlike most other hexAddress-typed fields in this schema, `address` is never null -- a string was found at some real address, there is no "address unknown" case for it (see StringRecord.__post_init__). `matched_grep` is a flag, not a filter: this record is emitted for every extracted string regardless of --grep -- null when no --grep was given at all (always null for --report's own notable_strings, which has no --grep concept), true/false per record when it was.

stringsSummary.description: Matches result.summary for kind == 'strings' (dumpex.commands.extract.collect_strings). Pins the scan-context fields the P2 review's own 'a zero-result scan must still be able to tell where the scan started' finding needs machine-enforced, not just documented/unit-tested -- requested_address is the only way to know the scan origin when `data.records` is empty. additionalProperties: false since these six fields are the whole of collect_strings' own summary dict today; a future field added there must extend this def too, the same way every other v2 record type is kept in lockstep with its Python producer.

reportThreadInfo.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportThreadInfo.to_dict() -- one thread as seen by --report, either the card's own anchor thread (Section 1) or one of the other threads sharing the anchor's resolved region (Section 3). `module_context` is null only when `start_address` is itself null (no address to resolve against). `backing_module_base`/`backing_module_end` are both-or-neither, and only ever non-null when `module_context == 'resolved'` -- Section 3's own 'other threads' entries never populate a range even when resolved (see the class's own docstring).

reportRegionInfo.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportRegionInfo.to_dict() -- the memory region resolved at a triage card's target address (Section 2). `file_offset` is a plain byte offset inside the .dmp file, not a process address, so it does NOT use hexAddress. `module_context`/`mz_header_detected`/`has_injected_pe` are a tri-state triple: `module_context` is never null (a resolved region always has SOME module-context answer); `mz_header_detected` is null iff the small header-peek read itself failed; `has_injected_pe` is null whenever the evidence needed to decide is itself missing (see the class's own docstring for the full derivation table, mirrored in the allOf below).

reportIocString.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportIocString.to_dict() -- one IOC-pattern string hit in a triage card's Section 4. `context_hex`/`context_base_address`/`context_hit_offset` are only ever populated when `is_network_pattern` is true -- a bounded (<=256 byte, i.e. <=512 hex char, enforced via context_hex's own maxLength) collect-time-computed hexdump-context window the renderer decodes instead of re-reading the dump (see dumpex.commands.report.render_report_console's own docstring for why). context_hit_offset's maximum of 255 is the loosest static bound this schema can express (the real constraint -- must fall strictly within THIS instance's own, possibly shorter, context_hex -- compares two sibling field values and is Python-only, see ReportIocString.__post_init__).

triageCardRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.TriageCardRecord.to_dict() -- one --report triage card. --report-string produces N cards (one per private-memory hit region) in one result.data.records list; --report-tid/--report-addr produce exactly one. `findings` is a closed, deduplicated vocabulary; `verdict` is cross-checked against len(findings) via the allOf below (0/1/2/3+ -> CLEAN/SUSPICIOUS/LIKELY_MALICIOUS/HIGH_CONFIDENCE_MALICIOUS), the same four-tier rule dumpex.core.memory.verdict_for() enforces in Python. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see TriageCardRecord.__post_init__): string_scan['truncated'] must equal bytes_read < requested_bytes, and findings/finding_details must name exactly the same keys -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES against each other within one object.

reportSummary.description: Matches result.summary for kind == 'report' (dumpex.commands.report.collect_report). `mode` says which of --report-tid/--report-addr/--report-string (or the tid+addr combination) produced this result -- the allOf below pins which query_* fields are required non-null per mode, the same way stringsSummary pins requested_address for --strings. `skipped_unreadable_regions`/`truncated_regions`/`clamped_regions` are StringSearchStats' own three counters (see dumpex.core.memory.StringSearchStats), always 0 outside string-search mode. additionalProperties: false since these twelve fields are the whole of collect_report's own summary dict today.

moduleDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ModuleDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed/rebased module between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_modules' own set logic. `name` is always a non-empty string ("(unnamed)" for an anonymous module -- see dumpex.commands.comparison._module_display_name), but full_path_before/full_path_after are only forced null on the side that genuinely has no entry -- the PRESENT side's full_path may legitimately be null too (an anonymous module has a real base_address but no name at all), so only base_address is required non-null for added/removed. `full_path_before`/`full_path_after` are otherwise unconstrained by change_type: address identifies a module diff, not path. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see ModuleDiffRecord.__post_init__): for `change_type: "rebased"`, base_address_before must differ from base_address_after -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES for inequality within one object.

threadDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ThreadDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed thread between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_threads' own TID-keyed set logic. backing_module_after/backing_module_context are only ever populated for 'added' (resolved against the TARGET's module list); diff_threads never attempts baseline-side module resolution for a removed thread. For 'added': backing_module_after/backing_module_context are both null exactly when start_address_after itself is null (module resolution is never attempted without a known address); otherwise backing_module_context is always one of resolved/unregistered/unavailable, and backing_module_after is non-null iff backing_module_context is 'resolved'.

memoryDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.MemoryDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed/protection-changed memory region between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_memory's own BaseAddress-keyed set logic. suspicious_before/_after reuse memoryRegionRecord.suspicious's own semantics rather than diff_memory's own 4-tier console categorization. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see MemoryDiffRecord.__post_init__): for `change_type: "protection_changed"`, protect_before must differ from protect_after -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES for inequality within one object.

comparisonRecord.description: Tagged union for result.kind == 'comparison' -- discriminated by entity_type, which is a distinct const on each branch.

kind.description: Which canonical record type result.data.records holds. Grows as more commands migrate onto v2 -- not an open string.

execution_status.description: Did the COMMAND itself run to completion -- independent of whether the EVIDENCE it saw was complete (see coverage below). 'partial' is used by --report when a self-imposed scan-budget clamp (MAX_REGION_READ) or a per-card --output write failure means the command didn't finish everything it set out to do, even though the evidence it DID look at may be fully covered.

status.description: Was the evidence available to this command complete? Vocabulary shared with dumpex.hunt._coverage.derive_coverage_status.

reasons.description: Backward-compatible flat human text, rendered from `limitations` -- kept so an existing consumer that only reads `reasons` never breaks.

sources.description: Per-source observed state -- keyed by source name (e.g. 'memory_info', 'threads', or a dotted entity-namespaced name such as 'baseline.modules' for a comparison result). Optional: an older producer that doesn't populate this is still a valid document.

limitations.description: Structured, machine-readable coverage gaps -- the source `reasons` is rendered from. `code` is intentionally a plain string, not a closed enum: dumpex.output.coverage.LimitationCode grows as commands migrate, and this schema should not need a version bump every time a new code is added.

summary.description: Free-form per-kind extension point by default (open object) -- refined per-kind via the allOf/if-then block below exactly like data.records is, wherever a kind's own summary fields carry machine-relevant facts (e.g. kind == 'strings'/'report', whose requested_address/query_* fields are the only way to know a zero-result scan's own origin).

diagnosticEntry.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.Diagnostic.to_dict(), which always emits all three fields -- `code` is required (it's always a key in the dict), just nullable.

sourceObservation.description: Matches dumpex.output.coverage.SourceObservation.to_dict(), which always emits all three fields -- `required` covers all of them, not just `state`, and the record_count<->state invariant (None for absent/failed, exactly 0 for present_empty, >=1 for present) is frozen structurally below, mirroring the same invariant SourceObservation.__post_init__ enforces in Python.

coverageLimitation.description: Matches dumpex.output.coverage.CoverageLimitation.to_dict(), which always emits every field regardless of `code` (null/[] where a given code doesn't use a field) -- `required` covers the full set for the same reason sourceObservation's does. `allOf` below constrains each KNOWN code's disallowed fields to their default (null/[]), pins `source` where fixed, and mirrors the value-shape rules dumpex.output.coverage._CODE_SPECS/CoverageLimitation.__post_init__ enforce that JSON Schema CAN express (minItems, exact array contents, non-null requirements, one-field-implies-another-field dependencies) -- each `if` matches only that one `code` value, so an unrecognized future code matches none of them and stays fully open; `code` itself remains a plain string, not an enum. This is NOT full parity with the Python model: rules comparing two field VALUES for inequality (source != counterpart_source) or against another object's state entirely outside this fragment (counterpart_source's own record_count, a sibling entry in result.coverage.sources) are Python-only and cannot be expressed here -- see CoverageLimitation.__post_init__ and _validate_source_absent_against_sources for those.

artifact.description: An output file the tool itself produced (e.g. an extracted memory region) -- distinct from meta.evidence, which describes the INPUT dump(s). Populated by --extract and --report (its own optional extract-to-file side effect, under a different `kind` string -- 'extracted_region' vs 'report_extracted_region'). Matches dumpex.output.records.Artifact.to_dict(), which always emits all six fields -- `required` covers all of them, not just id/kind/path.

finding.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._finding.Finding.to_dict() -- one hunter-agnostic judgment (facts/inference/confidence/rationale/limitations, tagged observation/lead/detection) inside a hunterRecord's `findings` array. yara is the one hunter that never populates this -- its own matches/rules_hit stay in YaraDetails instead (see hunterRecord's own allOf: findings must be [] for hunter == 'yara').

huntRegionRef.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntRegionRef.to_dict() -- a memory region reference inside a hunter's `details`, replacing the raw Region object v1.1 exposed via `_json_safe()`'s non-reproducible str(obj) fallback (see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md's cross-cutting finding #1). `base_address` is never null -- a region reference always names a real address.

huntThreadRef.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntThreadRef.to_dict() -- a TID plus optional StartAddress/current-instruction-pointer, hex-formatted. `ip`/`ip_reg` are both-or-neither: a thread reference either carries no live register snapshot (both null) or a real one (both set) -- there is no case where the register name is known but its value isn't, or vice versa.

huntThreadRegionHit.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntThreadRegionHit.to_dict() -- a thread correlated with a specific region, e.g. a thread's current RIP/EIP executing inside a flagged allocation, or its StartAddress falling inside one.

huntPeHeaderHit.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntPeHeaderHit.to_dict() -- one MZ-prefixed region examined for a hidden PE header, plus the structural-validation outcome. `entry_point_rva` stays a plain int (an RVA is relative to a not-yet-established image base, not itself a memory address); `image_base` (the PE header's OWN declared base) is a real address, hex-formatted. `reason` is set only when `valid` is false; every PE-fact field is set only when `valid` is true.

injectionDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.InjectionDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt injection`'s hunter-specific evidence. `pe_read_failed`/`pe_short_reads` deliberately do NOT appear here -- those are coverage counts, not evidence (see PE_HEADER_READ_FAILED/PE_HEADER_SHORT_READ limitations under this hunter's own coverage instead).

hollowingDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HollowingDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt hollowing`'s hunter-specific evidence: the four checks (memory type / MZ header / RWX protection at the image base, and the PEB-vs-module-list name compare). Unlike the other six hunters, every field here is a scalar -- there is no list-shaped evidence to break out into its own CSV table.

stompingDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.StompingDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt stomping`'s hunter-specific evidence. `protection_leads`/`verified_changes` entries are plain objects, not yet a dedicated typed shape (tracked follow-up -- see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md's stomping section) -- open objects here reflect that Python-side reality rather than inventing a contract the collector doesn't enforce yet.

pipeDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.PipeDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt pipe`'s hunter-specific evidence. Entries are plain objects, not yet a dedicated typed shape (tracked follow-up) -- same rationale as stompingDetails above.

csBeaconDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.CsBeaconDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt cs-beacon`'s hunter-specific evidence. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see CsBeaconDetails.__post_init__): config_count must equal len(configs).

yaraDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.YaraDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt yara`'s hunter-specific evidence. Deliberately off the shared `finding` model -- a YARA rule hit is a structural pattern match, not a check/facts/inference/confidence/rationale judgment.

obfuscationDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ObfuscationDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt obfuscation`'s hunter-specific evidence: the seven decode layers' own hit lists.

hunterRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HunterRecord.to_dict() -- one hunter's complete result, one entry in `result.data.records` for `result.kind == "hunt"`. `hunter` discriminates which of the 7 *Details types `details` must be (see the allOf below). `max_score`/`confidence`/`lead_count`/`review_priority` are null for every hunter except `hunter == "yara"`, where they must ALL be null -- never a mix of some set, some not (yara has none of these today, see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md's yara section). `coverage` is this ONE hunter's own CoverageReport, not the top-level `result.coverage` (which combines all selected hunters' reports -- see combine_coverage_reports()).

huntSummary.description: Matches result.summary for kind == 'hunt' -- the cross-hunter roll-up a single shared reducer computes (never re-derived independently by JSON/CSV/console -- see docs/hunt_migration_field_matrix.md's own summary-rules section). `selected` is the `--hunt` argument ("all" or one hunter name). `highest_verdict_level` is picked only from DETECTED hunters when any exist; otherwise it reflects the strongest non-detected signal (clean/inconclusive/not_evaluated).
